sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
Despite service of notice, no one appeared on behalf of the complainant.

2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.245 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376 (3),
323, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, Police Station Lalganj, District Pratapgarh.
3. The FIR in question was lodged as a missing person report.
Subsequently, in the statements under Sections 161 of Cr.P.C., the victim had stated that she had gone out of her own freewill with the applicant.
In the statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., she had gone with the applicant to Amrit Lal Verma vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ...

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mumbai, although, there are allegations of threat were also made, however, there is nothing to show that in the entire journey to Mumbai, she raised any hue and cry.
The tentative age of the victim as per the medical report is 15-16 years, however, there is no definite documents to demonstrate and conclude the issue of age at this stage.
4. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

5. Considering the aforesaid facts; the fact that prima facie the medical report also does not support the prosecution case, coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal history and is in custody since 20.08.2023, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Amrit Lal Verma be released on bail in the aforesaid first information report on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
